en: Taal Volcano is unique because it sits on Volcano Island inside Taal Lake, which is on the island of Luzon.
Mount Apo, located in Mindanao, is the highest mountain in the Philippines with an elevation of 2,954 meters above sea level.
The Philippine tarsier, found in Bohol, has enormous eyes that are actually larger than its entire brain.
The Cagayan River in Northern Luzon is the longest and largest river in the Philippines by volume and length.
Laguna de Bay, located east of Metro Manila, is the largest lake in the Philippines and a vital fishing ground.
The Underground River in Puerto Princesa, Palawan, is a UNESCO World Heritage site featuring a navigable subterranean river.
The waling-waling orchid, native to the rainforests of Mindanao, is widely considered the queen of Philippine orchids.
The Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park in the Sulu Sea protects over 600 species of fish and 360 species of coral.
The Philippines experiences the amihan, a cool northeast monsoon, which brings dry weather to most of the country from December to February.
The Chocolate Hills in Bohol consist of over 1,200 symmetrical limestone mounds that turn brown during the dry season.
The Banaue Rice Terraces in Ifugao province were carved into the mountains of the Philippine Cordilleras by indigenous farmers over 2,000 years ago.
The Philippine eagle, the national bird, is one of the largest and most powerful eagles in the world and is endemic to the country.
